query: How does choice of unit affect sample size calculations and claims of generalisability for policy recommendations?

response.query: How does choice of unit affect sample size calculations and claims of generalisability for policy recommendations?
response.answer: Choice of unit affects sample size calculations by determining the number of subjects or observations. Larger samples improve generalisability of policy recommendations. Smaller, non-representative samples limit generalisability.

results.title: Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor ...
results.content: Docket Title | Document ID | Comments || Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings | OSHA-2021-0009-4761 | 43,437 |  |. OSHA estimates that a heat emergency will require less time from a designated person because, in a heat emergency, the affected employee will be transported to a medical facility by EMS rather than monitored for the duration at the work site. Supplemental trainings would also be required for at-risk workers when either (1) worker(s) heat exposure changes, (2) policies and procedures change, (3) worker(s) does not retain information, or (4) a heat-related injury or illness occurs that results in death, days away from work, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness. The role of workplace incentives in the labor productivity effects of heat exposure is discussed later in section VIII.I.III.B.
